name: Supabase Realtime
solves: Provides WebSocket-based real-time functionality including broadcasting ephemeral messages between clients, tracking and synchronizing shared presence state, and streaming Postgres database changes (inserts, updates, deletes) to authorized clients.
best_for: Supabase-based apps needing real-time database change notifications without polling
Collaborative apps requiring presence tracking (e.g., who's online, cursor positions)
Multiplayer features like shared cursors, live avatars, or typing indicators via ephemeral broadcast
Apps already using Supabase Auth and Postgres that want real-time features with row-level security
Building notification or activity feed systems triggered by Postgres row changes
skip_when: You need guaranteed message delivery — Supabase Realtime does not guarantee every message reaches every client
Your project has no Postgres database and you only need pub/sub between clients (consider Pusher, Ably, or Socket.IO instead)
You need sub-10ms ultra-low-latency messaging for gaming or trading (dedicated real-time brokers like Ably or custom WebSocket servers are better)
You want a lightweight self-contained WebSocket library without an opinionated backend stack (use ws or Socket.IO)
Your infrastructure cannot run the Elixir/Phoenix server and you don't want to use Supabase's hosted platform

hosted_alternative.name: Supabase Platform
hosted_alternative.pricing_summary: Free tier includes 200 concurrent connections and 2M messages/month; Pro plan at $25/mo includes 500 connections and 5M messages; usage-based beyond that
